newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares ease, further declines seen.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares ease, further declines seen.

text.p: Slovenia's SBI index eased almost one percent on Wednesday pulled down by losses in drug firm Lek, and traders said the downside looked set to continue.
The SBI index fell 14.11 points to 1,544.29. Overall eight shares fell, 10 rose, two were unchanged and eight were untraded. Turnover firmed to 203.9 million tolars from 170.7 million.
The index has fallen 2.5 percent in the past two days, after a 7.7 percent jump the previous week.
Drug firm Lek was the most actively traded share, down 2.97 percent to 35,000 tolars on volume of 2,703 shares.

Traders mainly attributed Lek's fall to a slump in international demand as most foreigners had already bought the number of Lek shares they wanted in their portfolio. International investors hold about 22 percent of Lek.
Lek could slide to 33,000 in the next couple of weeks if international demand did not improve, the traders added.

Dealers said the SBI index could drop to 1,500 points by the middle of next week if international demand remained low, adding foreigners were probably waiting for half year results before they bought any more stock.
"A lot depends on international investors as domestic buyers are much more active when they know foreign demand is high," a broker said.
Brokerage Dadas led decliners, closing 10.17 percent lower at 5,390 on volume of five shares and traders attributed the fall to a lack of liquidity.

Preferred shares of bank Hipoterna Banka Brezice were top gainers, up 10 percent to 3,300 on volume of 10 shares. Traders said the share remained very illiquid therefore its gains could be short-lived.
